name: TF-Luna LiDAR distance sensor
description: Benewake single-point time-of-flight LiDAR: measures distance from 0.2 to 8 m (1 cm resolution, ±6 cm up to 3 m) and streams it over a 3.3 V UART at 115200 baud, 100 frames per second by default (I2C mode when pin 5 is grounded). Needs a 3.7–5.2 V supply. Sold as: Benewake TF-Luna LiDAR module with its 6-wire GH1.25 cable (+5V, RXD/SDA, TXD/SCL, GND, CONFIG, MUX), UART mode with CONFIG left open.
eli5: Shines an invisible laser at whatever is in front of it and tells your board how far away it is, in centimetres.

pins.name: +5V
pins.description: Supply, 3.7–5.2 V (use the 5 V / VBUS pin; 3.3 V is too low). Up to 150 mA peak.

pins.name: RXD/SDA
pins.description: UART receive (commands from the board's TX), 3.3 V logic. SDA in I2C mode.

pins.name: TXD/SCL
pins.description: UART transmit (distance frames to the board's RX), 3.3 V logic. SCL in I2C mode.

pins.name: CONFIG
pins.description: Configuration input (pin 5): leave open or tie to 3.3 V for UART mode; ground selects I2C mode.

pins.name: MUX
pins.description: Multiplexing output (pin 6): on/off-mode output, or data-ready in I2C mode. Not used in UART mode.

buildNotes: Power it from 5 V (VBUS/VIN), not 3V3: the supply range is 3.7–5.2 V. Signals are 3.3 V LVTTL, so TXD/RXD connect straight to ESP32/Pico pins.
Leave pin 5 (CONFIG) unconnected for UART mode. Grounding it switches the sensor to I2C (address 0x10) and the serial frames stop.
Cross the serial lines: sensor TXD → board RX, sensor RXD → board TX. 115200 baud, 8N1.
Default output: 9-byte frame 59 59 DistL DistH AmpL AmpH TempL TempH Sum at 100 Hz. Sum = low byte of bytes 0..7; distance in cm; temperature = Temp/8 − 256 °C.
Distance is unreliable when Amp < 100 (too weak, reported as 0 cm) or Amp = 65535 (overexposed); readings under 20 cm are in the blind zone.
No reverse-polarity or over-voltage protection: check the +5V/GND wires before powering up.

driver.code:
# Benewake TF-Luna LiDAR distance sensor, UART mode (pin 5 left open), MicroPython driver.
# From the TF-Luna user manual (Benewake, REV 01/04/2024): 115200 baud 8N1; by default the
# sensor streams the 9-byte/cm frame 100 times a second:
#   0x59 0x59 Dist_L Dist_H Amp_L Amp_H Temp_L Temp_H Checksum
# Checksum = low 8 bits of the sum of bytes 0..7. Dist in cm, Amp = signal strength,
# chip temperature = Temp / 8 - 256 degC. Dist is unreliable when Amp < 100 or Amp == 65535.
import time


class TFLuna:
    def __init__(self, uart):
        self.uart = uart  # UART(id, baudrate=115200, tx=..., rx=...)

    def read(self, timeout_ms=500):
        """Wait for the next valid frame; return (distance_cm, amp, temperature_C)."""
        self.uart.read()  # drop stale frames queued since the last call
        buf = b''
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < timeout_ms:
            n = self.uart.any()
            if n:
                buf += self.uart.read(n)
            while len(buf) >= 9:
                if buf[0] == 0x59 and buf[1] == 0x59 and (sum(buf[0:8]) & 0xFF) == buf[8]:
                    dist = buf[2] | (buf[3] << 8)
                    amp = buf[4] | (buf[5] << 8)
                    temp = (buf[6] | (buf[7] << 8)) / 8 - 256
                    return dist, amp, temp
                buf = buf[1:]  # not a frame start (or bad checksum): resync
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        raise OSError('TF-Luna: no valid frame (check TXD wiring, 115200 baud, pin 5 not grounded)')

    def distance(self):
        """Distance in cm, or None when the signal is too weak or overexposed."""
        d, amp, _ = self.read()
        return None if amp < 100 or amp == 0xFFFF else d

    def _cmd(self, body):
        frame = bytes([0x5A, len(body) + 3]) + bytes(body)
        self.uart.write(frame + bytes([sum(frame) & 0xFF]))

    def set_frame_rate(self, hz):
        """ID_SAMPLE_FREQ (0x03): 1..250 Hz, 0 = trigger mode. Not saved until save()."""
        self._cmd([0x03, hz & 0xFF, hz >> 8])

    def save(self):
        """ID_SAVE_SETTINGS (0x11)."""
        self._cmd([0x11])

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from tfluna import TFLuna

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=115200, tx=Pin({RXD_SDA}), rx=Pin({TXD_SCL}))
lidar = TFLuna(uart)
while True:
    d, amp, t = lidar.read()
    print('D=%dcm AMP=%d T=%.1fC' % (d, amp, t))
    time.sleep_ms(500)
